properties.title: Scanning While Imagining: A Scene-Graph World Model for Robotic Ultrasound Navigation

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Scene-graph world model and receding-horizon planner for robotic ultrasound probe navigation, evaluated on four held-out CT cases and 19 phantom trials.
Transformer scene-graph and pose world model with a sampled-candidate, recursive-imagination, shortest-path planner that replans from observed scene graphs.
properties.implementation_stage: evaluation (simulated CT-derived environments and one physical phantom)
properties.world_model_status: core world model, action- and goal-conditioned

properties.algorithm: Transformer encoder-decoder over scene-graph and pose history, candidate action and goal set (d = 384, H = 10 history, K = 10 future pairs)

properties.population: abdominal anatomy from CT label maps and an abdominal ultrasound phantom
properties.decision: selection of probe motions toward an acceptable target view for gallbladder or pancreas

properties.description: 24 patient CT cases with CADS anatomical label maps, 1,839 generated probe trajectories, 63,164 waypoints; 20 training and 4 test cases
Four patient-disjoint held-out CT cases (7,981 test samples) used for prediction and closed-loop navigation in simulation
19 robot trials on the US-22 abdominal phantom with scene graphs generated from a registered phantom label map
Scene-graph prediction over 20 steps and closed-loop navigation with execution horizons 1, 5 and 10 on four held-out CT cases
Robot phantom navigation with label-map-derived observations

assertions.rationale: CADS label maps from 24 patient CT cases, generated trajectories, manually validated target views and a patient-disjoint split are documented, although the origin of the labels for each case is not detailed here.
Waypoints are indexed by step and no acquisition times are given.
No availability times are described.
No missing-data indicators are described.
No measurement staleness is described.
Fixed discrete steps are used and irregular sampling is not discussed.
No observation process is modelled.
No timestamp audit is reported.

criteria_met: A fixed graph schema with at most seven nodes
Training-set normalization of actions and pose translations
criteria_missing: A cross-protocol or cross-site harmonization audit
assertions.rationale: Schema and normalization only.
The split is patient-disjoint, normalization and the goal threshold use training cases only, and goal poses are hidden from the planner.
No federated arrangement is described.
A shared scene-graph encoder produces a node and pair embedding, and poses are encoded from a 9-D representation.
No pretrained encoder is described.
The loss predicts explicit scene-graph and pose targets, not a latent representation.
No collapse control is described.
No reconstruction test is reported.
A multilayer perceptron fuses scene-graph and pose embeddings and the Transformer attends over history, action and goal tokens.
No missing-modality handling is described.
The latest H = 10 scene-graph and pose pairs are carried into each prediction and updated with new observations, and closed-loop navigation was run with them.
No distribution over hidden state is maintained.

criteria_met: Eight candidate trajectories from the same history are imagined and compared, and shown in Figure 4
criteria_missing: Quantitative comparison of predicted successors across alternatives
assertions.rationale: Qualitative display only.
No ordering or irreversibility constraint is described.
Future scene graphs and poses are predicted for up to 20 steps and scored on four held-out cases.
The transition is learned from CT-derived sequences with a Transformer encoder and decoder.
Candidate motions condition the first transition and closed-loop success is reported, but the action input is not ablated.
A deterministic predictor is described and no sampled outputs are reported.
No mechanistic model is described.
No mechanistic component is combined with the learned transition.
No multi-backend contract is described.
No coupled scales are described.
Each of K = 10 predicted pairs is supervised by its future waypoint, although training is parallel over a chunk and not recursive.
Chunked prediction is described without a hierarchy of timescales.
Decoded tokens produce graph outputs and poses and no ultrasound images are synthesized.
Scene-graph and pose heads read each decoded token.
First-step scene graphs are compared with reference graphs from held-out label maps, with relation F1 of 94.45 and 94.89 and BBox mIoU below 43 percent.
A recursive extension uses predicted history without new observations and is scored to step 20.
The training regime for recursive rollout is not described.
Newly observed scene graphs correct history before replanning and replanning after every step gave the highest success.
The furthest evaluated prediction extent is 20 steps.
Relation F1 falls from 94.45 to 93.59 while node visibility F1 and BBox mIoU fall more, across steps 1 to 20.
No acceptance tolerance or supported horizon is stated and accuracy beyond 20 steps is uncharacterized.
Candidate branches differ by action and no sampled futures for the same action are reported.
The imagination limit of 300 states is far beyond the evaluated 20 steps and no supported-horizon policy is stated.
Imagined branches are compared before execution and the selected motion is run in closed loop.
Eight perturbed candidate motions are rolled out recursively and the shortest goal-reaching branch is selected, with reported success rates and no baseline planner.
The plan is recomputed from observed scene graphs after executing a prefix, with execution horizons of 1, 5 and 10 steps compared.
The world model is trained with graph and pose losses and the planner separately minimizes predicted translational path length.
No uncertainty is used in planning.
No test of whether the planner exploits model errors is reported.

gate_assessments.rationale: Patient-disjoint splitting (20 train / 4 test CADS CT cases), training-only normalization/thresholds, and hidden goal poses are described, but per-case CADS label origins/demographics are unreported, observations are label-map-derived rather than B-mode ultrasound images, case-specific CT goal scene graphs (G_goal) are supplied for held-out patients, and data provenance/leakage assertions remain at specification stage.

1-to-20-step scene-graph prediction is evaluated on 4 held-out CT label-map cases with high spatial relation F1 (94.45%–94.89% at step 1; 93.59%–94.19% at step 20), but BBox mIoU is low and declining (39.92%–42.44% at step 1 to 31.58%–34.09% at step 20; test_outcome='mixed' on assertion:B042:0053), and observations are label-map-derived rather than ultrasound images.
Drift is measured to step 20 but no effective horizon is established, accuracy beyond 20 steps is uncharacterized, and the planner imagines up to 300 states.
Candidates are random perturbations with no support check and the comparison of predicted successors is shown only qualitatively in Figure 4.
Closed-loop success is reported, but no baseline policy is compared, the planner is not tested against model-error exploitation and the authors state no design contribution was isolated.
A surface constraint, invalid-state termination and a no-goal fallback are described, but no guard is evaluated and no fail behavior or escalation is defined.
Success is reported in simulation and on a phantom but the tasks are not matched and no agreement or bias is quantified, and no human evaluation exists.

legacy_cells.B: Scanning While Imagining: A Scene-Graph World Model for Robotic Ultrasound Navigation
legacy_cells.C: Li, Xuesong, Chen, Shuai, Li, Feng, Jiang, Zhongliang, Navab, Nassir, Bi, Yuan
legacy_cells.O: Abdominal ultrasound target-view acquisition for gallbladder and pancreas anatomy
legacy_cells.S: Can an action- and goal-conditioned scene-graph model predict anatomical view changes and guide probe motions to an acceptable ultrasound target view?
legacy_cells.T: 24 patient CT cases: 20 training and four patient-disjoint test cases; abdominal phantom navigation was also tested.
legacy_cells.V: Select probe motions expected to reach a goal ultrasound view, and verify target-view acquisition from observed scene graphs.
legacy_cells.AI: CT-label-map-derived anatomical scene graphs; probe poses; candidate probe-motion actions; goal scene graphs
legacy_cells.AJ: Shared scene-graph encoder; MLP fuses graph and pose embeddings; Transformer encoder-decoder with scene-graph and pose prediction heads
legacy_cells.AM: MLP fuses scene-graph and probe-pose embeddings; Transformer attends over history, candidate-action, and goal tokens
legacy_cells.AZ: Anatomical scene graph with fixed organ identities, per-node geometry/visibility attributes, and explicit spatial relations; predicted poses are also represented.
legacy_cells.BD: Six-dimensional local probe motion: translation in mm and rotation vector in rad
legacy_cells.BL: 10 observed SG–pose history pairs; 10 future pairs per prediction chunk; results evaluate up to 20 recursively predicted steps.
legacy_cells.BN: Fixed anatomical node identities; structured scene-graph nodes, geometric attributes, and relations (adjacent to, left of, superficial to); trajectories constrained to the body surface.
legacy_cells.BP: H = 10 observed SG–pose pairs; the latest H pairs are retained in the history.
legacy_cells.BS: Future anatomical scene graphs (node presence, attributes, pair features, spatial relations) and probe poses; no ultrasound images are synthesized.
legacy_cells.BT: Scene-graph prediction head and probe-pose prediction head
legacy_cells.BU: Planner minimizes predicted cumulative translational travel distance to a goal-matching branch (mm); no learned reward/value model is described.
legacy_cells.BV: L = LSG + Lpose; graph loss combines binary cross-entropy for presence and relations, SmoothL1 for node attributes and pair features, and component-count regression; pose loss penalizes translation and rotation errors.
legacy_cells.CD: 20 predicted steps evaluated; planner imagination limit is 300 predicted states.
legacy_cells.CI: 300 predicted states maximum (30 chunks of K = 10)
legacy_cells.CK: Choose the shortest predicted translational path among branches whose predicted scene graph matches a goal graph; execute one or more steps and replan from new observations.
legacy_cells.DN: CADS CT volumes and anatomical label maps; US-22 CT/US abdominal phantom
legacy_cells.DQ: 24 patient CT cases; 1,839 generated trajectories and 63,164 waypoints; 53,344 training samples and 7,981 test samples; 19 robot–phantom trials.
legacy_cells.DX: At one prediction step: gallbladder node-visibility F1 88.74%, spatial-relation F1 94.45%, BBox mIoU 39.92%; pancreas 93.13%, 94.89%, and 42.44%, respectively.
legacy_cells.DY: At steps 1 to 20, gallbladder-conditioned relation F1 94.45% to 93.59%, node-visibility F1 88.74% to 82.70%, and BBox mIoU 39.92% to 31.58%; pancreas-conditioned values were 94.89% to 94.19%, 93.13% to 87.50%, and 42.44% to 34.09%.
legacy_cells.EC: Closed-loop CT navigation with Execute 1 succeeded in 93/120 gallbladder trials (77.50%) and 90/120 pancreas trials (75.00%); robot–phantom navigation succeeded in 14/19 trials (73.7%).
legacy_cells.EK: No component ablation reported; the authors state that evaluation assesses the complete system without isolating individual design contributions.
legacy_cells.EL: Prediction visibility and bounding-box overlap declined with rollout horizon; longer execution horizons reduced navigation success, especially for far starts (pancreas success 16.36% at Execute 5 and 10.91% at Execute 10).
legacy_cells.EM: Probe execution used a surface constraint and a compliant position–force controller with workspace limits; when no branch reaches a predicted goal, the planner returns NO GOAL REACHED without selecting a trajectory.
legacy_cells.FL: A shared scene-graph encoder and pose embedding feed a Transformer encoder-decoder conditioned on history, a candidate first motion, and goal graphs. Scene-graph and pose heads predict future state pairs; a recursive planner simulates branches, scores goal-reaching paths, executes a short horizon, then replans from observations.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes SonoGraph-WM for joint prediction of anatomical scene graphs and probe poses; introduces CT-label-map-derived SG–pose training sequences; evaluates prediction, closed-loop CT navigation, and robotic phantom navigation.
legacy_cells.FN: On four held-out CT cases, spatial-relation F1 remained above 93% through 20 prediction steps. Execute-1 CT navigation succeeded in 77.50% of gallbladder and 75.00% of pancreas trials; phantom navigation succeeded in 14/19 trials (73.7%).
legacy_cells.FO: Only four CT test anatomies were evaluated; prediction accuracy beyond 20 steps is uncharacterized despite a 300-state planning limit; the study does not test B-mode-to-scene-graph perception or perception errors during navigation; goal graphs are case-specific; individual design contributions were not isolated.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors identify extending the approach to B-mode input with a schema-compatible scene-graph estimator and evaluating perception errors, and using cross-subject goal representations to reduce reliance on case-specific reference graphs.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that existing robotic ultrasound methods generally do not explicitly predict how anatomy evolves along candidate paths, while prior scene-graph guidance is coarse and does not specify executable robot motions.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports CT-supervised scene-graph prediction and probe navigation in held-out CT-derived cases plus a small abdominal-phantom study, not B-mode perception, prospective clinical evaluation, patient benefit, or broad clinical deployment. Rollout fidelity was evaluated only through 20 steps; the 300-state limit is a planning cap, not a validated prediction horizon. Action conditioning concerns probe acquisition, not identified treatment effects.

notes:
Scene-graph world model for robotic ultrasound navigation. A Transformer predicts future anatomical scene graphs and probe poses from a history of ten pairs, a candidate motion and a goal set, and a planner samples eight candidate motions, imagines each branch recursively and selects the shortest goal-reaching path. Trained on CT-label-map-derived sequences from 24 cases and evaluated on four held-out cases (prediction to step 20, closed-loop success 77.50 and 75.00 percent with replanning every step) and on a phantom (14 of 19 trials). Classified L4 and core with narrow scope. Source points: observations come from label maps and not ultrasound images, no baseline or ablation, success falls to 22.50 to 40.83 percent with 5 or 10 step execution, accuracy beyond 20 steps uncharacterized, no uncertainty.

Targeted source gap-review addendum (2026-11-22): Figures 1-3 confirm the candidate-action/goal SG planner, CT-label supervision, joint SG/pose prediction, and anatomical node attributes/relations. Ultrasound images in Figure 1 are explicitly illustrative. Page 8 limitations retain the small four-anatomy evaluation, annotation-derived SG inputs, and uncharacterized prediction accuracy beyond 20 steps despite the planning cap of 300.
